--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.cmty_louvain_levels()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: >- Return the community partition at each level of the Louvain algorithm. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.cmty_louvain_levels()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: >- Return the community partition at each level of the Louvain algorithm. title: >- [Graph.cmty_louvain_levels()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- Return the community partition at each level of the Louvain algorithm. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Return the community partition at each level of the Louvain algorithm. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L45767-L45874){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.cmty_louvain_levels( resolution=1.0, seed=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Louvain community levels](../assets/graphs/cmty-louvain-levels.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="A two-by-four ladder, A to D on top and E to H below. Left, Louvain's first level (seed 0) pairs neighbors along the rails into four communities, A, B in the accent color, C, D in teal, E, F in violet and G, H in gold. Right, the next level merges those pairs into two communities, the left half A, B, E, F (accent) and the right half C, D, G, H (teal)." width="100%"} Louvain builds communities bottom-up: it first groups nodes into small communities, then collapses each community into a single node and repeats on the smaller graph. Each round gives a coarser partition, so the levels form a hierarchy, from many small groups to a few large ones. `cmty_louvain()` keeps only the last level; this method returns all of them, to explore communities at several scales (neighborhoods within districts, teams within departments). The graph must be undirected. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [resolution]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1.0]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Resolution parameter (default 1); larger values favor smaller communities. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Random seed for the node visiting order. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[dict[int, int]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : One node-to-community dictionary per level, finest first. Labels are numbered in order of the lowest node ID in each community. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is directed. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Each level is one round of local moving (the fast queue-based variant) followed by aggregation; a level is recorded whenever the partition is coarser than the previous one, and the run stops when no node moves. `cmty_louvain()` is a separate implementation with a fixed visiting order, so its partition can differ from the last level here. Mirrors NetworkX's `louvain_partitions` (which yields lists of node sets). ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~cmty_louvain`) : The final partition only, from a separate implementation. [](`~cmty_leiden_levels`) : The same levels with Leiden's refinement step. [](`~modularity`) : The score that each level raises. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Twelve triangles in a ring, each joined to the next by one edge. The first level finds the twelve triangles. The second merges neighboring triangles in pairs, which scores a higher modularity even though each pair is plainly two groups (modularity's resolution limit): ::: {#6ac3eb07 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_ring_of_cliques(12, 3) levels = graph.cmty_louvain_levels(seed=5) [ (len(set(level.values())), round(graph.modularity(level), 3)) for level in levels ] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` [(12, 0.667), (6, 0.708)] ``` ::: ::: ### Two scales in *Les Misérables* `les_miserables()` links two characters of Victor Hugo's novel when they appear in the same chapter. Louvain finds 10 communities at its first level and merges them into 6 at the second: ::: {#a79c646a .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} miserables = ec.les_miserables() levels = miserables.cmty_louvain_levels(seed=1) [ (len(set(level.values())), round(miserables.modularity(level), 3)) for level in levels ] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` [(10, 0.523), (6, 0.565)] ``` ::: ::: Each community of the second level (right) is one or more of the first (left). The Gillenormands and the Pontmercys join the community around Valjean, Cosette and Marius, and the Patron-Minette gang joins the Thénardiers: ::: {layout-ncol="2"} ::: {#28e16b75 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} miserables.set_node_attrs("level_0", levels[0]) miserables.plot( color_by="level_0", edge_color_by="level_0", show_labels=False, seed=3, width=320, height=360, legend=False, ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
